title: React Knowledge Check
description: Test your React knowledge with these 40 interview questions covering hooks, state, lifecycle, and more.

questions.question: What is the virtual DOM in React?
options: A direct copy of the real DOM stored in memory
A lightweight in-memory representation of the real DOM used to optimize updates
A server-side rendered version of the DOM
A browser API provided by modern browsers

questions.question: Which hook is used to perform side effects in a functional component?
options: useState
useContext
useEffect
useReducer

questions.question: What does the second argument of useEffect do?
options: Sets the initial state value
Specifies the dependency array to control when the effect runs
Defines cleanup logic for the effect
Provides a callback after the component mounts

questions.question: What is a controlled component in React?
options: A component rendered by a parent without props
A component whose form data is handled by the component state
A component that controls other components via context
A component that uses the ref API

questions.question: What hook would you use to access a value from React Context?
options: useRef
useContext
useReducer
useMemo

questions.question: What does React.memo do?
options: Memoizes a function so it is not recreated on every render
Creates a memoized version of a value
Wraps a component to prevent re-renders if props have not changed
Provides a cache for asynchronous data

questions.question: Which hook returns a memoized callback function?
options: useMemo
useCallback
useEffect
useRef

questions.question: What is the purpose of the key prop in a list?
options: To add CSS styles to list items
To help React identify which items have changed, are added, or removed
To pass unique data between sibling components
To define the tab order of elements

questions.question: What does useRef return?
options: A state variable and a setter function
A mutable ref object whose .current property is persisted across renders
A context object
A callback function

questions.question: Which lifecycle method is equivalent to useEffect with an empty dependency array?
options: componentDidUpdate
componentWillUnmount
componentDidMount
shouldComponentUpdate

questions.question: What is prop drilling?
options: Passing data directly through a portal
A performance optimization technique
Passing props through multiple nested components to reach a deeply nested child
An anti-pattern for using context

questions.question: What is the difference between state and props?
options: State is read-only, props are mutable
Props are internal, state is passed from parent
State is managed internally by a component, props are passed from a parent
There is no difference

questions.question: What does React.lazy do?
options: Delays state updates to batch them together
Allows you to render a dynamic import as a regular component for code splitting
Creates a lazy-evaluated context value
Memoizes expensive computations

questions.question: What is Suspense used for in React?
options: To suspend component re-renders during heavy computations
To display a fallback while waiting for something (lazy load or data fetch) to resolve
To delay side effects until after the paint
To create deferred state updates

questions.question: What is the correct way to update state based on its previous value?
options: setState(state + 1)
setState((prev) => prev + 1)
state = state + 1
setState(this.state + 1)

questions.question: What is reconciliation in React?
options: The process of syncing state with the server
The algorithm React uses to diff the virtual DOM and update the real DOM efficiently
Converting JSX to JavaScript
Merging multiple context providers

questions.question: What does the useReducer hook return?
options: A memoized value and a cache function
A ref object and a dispatch function
The current state and a dispatch function
A context and a provider

questions.question: When should you use useReducer instead of useState?
options: When you want to avoid re-renders
When state logic is complex or the next state depends on the previous one with multiple sub-values
When you need to access the DOM
When sharing state across multiple components

questions.question: What is a React Fragment?
options: A way to split code into smaller bundles
A wrapper that lets you group elements without adding an extra DOM node
A component lifecycle hook
A memoized version of a child component

questions.question: What is the purpose of React portals?
options: To share state across multiple applications
To render children into a DOM node outside the parent component's DOM hierarchy
To create global context
To lazy-load components

questions.question: What is Error Boundary in React?
options: A hook that catches promise rejections
A class component that catches JavaScript errors in its child tree and displays a fallback UI
A try-catch block for functional components
A context that propagates error states

questions.question: What does JSX stand for?
options: JavaScript XML
Java Syntax Extension
JavaScript Extra
JSON Syntax for XML

questions.question: Which method is called when a component is removed from the DOM?
options: componentDidMount
componentDidUpdate
componentWillUnmount
componentWillReceiveProps

questions.question: What is the default value of the React context if no Provider is above it?
options: null
undefined
The value passed to createContext()
An empty object {}

questions.question: What does forwardRef do?
options: Forwards props to child components automatically
Allows a parent to pass a ref to a child component's DOM element
Creates a ref that persists in a forward cache
Forwards context to nested consumers

questions.question: What is the purpose of useMemo?
options: To memoize a callback function reference
To persist values across renders without causing re-renders
To memoize the result of an expensive computation so it only re-runs when dependencies change
To memo-ize component trees

questions.question: What is React Fiber?
options: A new CSS-in-JS library used with React
A reimplementation of React's core algorithm enabling incremental rendering
A server-side rendering framework
A file bundler optimized for React

questions.question: What is the strict mode in React used for?
options: To enforce TypeScript types in JSX
To enable production optimizations
To highlight potential problems in an application by activating extra checks and warnings
To restrict component re-renders

questions.question: How do you prevent a component from re-rendering when its parent re-renders?
options: Use useEffect with an empty dependency array
Wrap the component with React.memo
Use useRef instead of useState
Use dangerouslySetInnerHTML

questions.question: What is the purpose of the children prop?
options: To pass state from child to parent
To allow a component to render whatever is passed between its opening and closing tags
To list sub-components in a parent
To define default props

questions.question: What will happen if you call setState inside render?
options: The state updates silently without re-rendering
React will batch the update for the next cycle
It causes an infinite loop of re-renders
It throws a compile-time error

questions.question: What does the useLayoutEffect hook do differently from useEffect?
options: It runs only once on mount
It fires synchronously after all DOM mutations but before the browser paints
It runs asynchronously after the browser paints
It is used for CSS layout calculations only

questions.question: What is server-side rendering (SSR) in the context of React?
options: Rendering React components to a string on the server and sending HTML to the client
Using a Node.js server to manage React state
Pre-fetching API data before mounting components
Rendering only the server components and skipping the client bundle

questions.question: What is hydration in React?
options: Adding CSS variables to a React component
Loading remote data into the component state
The process of attaching event listeners to server-rendered HTML on the client
Converting static HTML to a React component tree

questions.question: Which prop is used to conditionally apply CSS classes in React?
options: style
className
class
cssClass

questions.question: What is the purpose of the useImperativeHandle hook?
options: To imperatively update the DOM
To customize the instance value exposed to parent components when using ref
To override React's reconciliation algorithm
To bypass prop validation

questions.question: What is the difference between an uncontrolled and a controlled input in React?
options: Uncontrolled inputs use useState; controlled inputs use useRef
Controlled inputs store their value in React state; uncontrolled inputs let the DOM manage the value
Uncontrolled inputs are read-only; controlled inputs accept user input
There is no functional difference

questions.question: What does the spread operator do when used in JSX like <Component {...props}>?
options: It deep-clones the props object
It passes all properties of the props object as individual props to the component
It merges the component's default props with the passed props
It converts props to a string

questions.question: What is the purpose of the displayName property on a React component?
options: To set the title shown in the browser tab
To label the component in React DevTools for easier debugging
To display a label above the rendered component
To set the component's accessible name

questions.question: Which React hook would you use to subscribe to an external store (e.g., Zustand, Redux)?
options: useContext
useEffect
useSyncExternalStore
useReducer
